sources.title: Kalshi API documentation index (llms.txt)
sources.verified: Index of official endpoint pages used below.

sources.title: API environments and endpoints
sources.verified: Demo REST base https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (recommended) and https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (also supported). Demo WebSocket wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 and wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2. Demo and production credentials are separate.
sources.notes: Matches the endpoints in the project brief.

sources.title: Get Markets (OpenAPI)
sources.verified: Filter status enum: unopened, open, paused, closed, settled. Market.status enum: initialized, inactive, active, closed, determined, disputed, amended, finalized. result enum: yes, no, scalar, blank. limit max 1000; tickers filter returns all matches in one response; mve_filter=exclude; volume_fp and volume_24h_fp are contract counts (no dollar-volume field); notional_value_dollars present.
sources.notes: The API returns status values active and finalized; the filter uses open and settled. Recorded as an irregularity in the review.

sources.title: Get Market Candlesticks
sources.verified: GET /series/{series_ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks. period_interval must be 1, 60 or 1440 minutes. start_ts/end_ts in seconds. Max 5,000 periods per request. Candle fields: end_period_ts, price{open,high,low,close,...}_dollars, yes_bid{}, yes_ask{}, volume_fp, open_interest_fp. Settled markets before the historical cutoff must use /historical/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks.
sources.notes: Seconds-level candles are not offered; live seconds in the site come from polling.

sources.title: Get Market Orderbook
sources.verified: Returns resting bids only: yes_dollars and no_dollars arrays of [price, count]; ascending order; best bid is the last element. No authentication needed. Unknown tickers return empty arrays, not 404.

sources.title: Orderbook responses (binary market mechanics)
sources.verified: YES ask = 1.00 minus best NO bid; NO ask = 1.00 minus best YES bid.
sources.notes: Used to compute the implied asks shown on the site.

sources.title: Fixed-point representation
sources.verified: *_dollars fields are fixed-point dollar strings (up to 4 decimals in requests, up to 6 in responses); *_fp fields are contract counts with 2 decimals. Price grids come from price_ranges.
sources.notes: The site parses them as numbers and keeps the official string precision where it matters.

sources.title: Market settlement
sources.verified: Yes outcome pays $1 per Yes contract; No outcome pays $1 per No contract. Settlement timing can vary. Settlement fees are zero for simple yes/no determinations.
sources.notes: Used for the simulated payoff in the strategy lab.

sources.title: Historical data and cutoffs
sources.verified: Settled markets older than the market_settled_ts cutoff move to /historical/markets. Live /markets stops returning them after the cutoff. Cutoff at check time: market_settled_ts 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z.
sources.notes: Resolved window (30 days) is inside the live range.

sources.title: Rate limits and tiers
sources.verified: Requests are token-metered. Unauthenticated public requests have separate limits; back off on HTTP 429.
sources.notes: The unauthenticated limit figure is not published on that page. The browser backs off on 429.

sources.title: WebSocket quick start (authentication)
sources.verified: WebSocket connections require authentication during the handshake, even for public channels such as ticker and trade.
sources.notes: Streaming is therefore not used by this site.
